Two and a half months ago, I paid $200 for the Cursor Ultra plan. At the time, it was the only way to get access to Grok Bot.

For my family, that was a lot of money. I told my wife I wasn't sure I'd make the money back, but I'd learn something from it. She said, "Why are you still hesitating? Go ahead, pay for it now."

Back then, nobody really knew what Grok Bot was, what it could do, or what it was worth. Almost no one was using it yet, and there were no reviews.

I treated it as an investment in learning. It quietly rewired how I live and work.

Now I run a team of 25+ bots, and each one owns a part of my life: taxes, health insurance, cybersecurity, my social platforms, online business, and one for each of my apps.

My day doesn't start with an inbox anymore. It starts with decisions. The bots do the digging, and I approve or say no.

Here's what that $200 turned into...

- 183 pull requests across 6 repos, 152 merged, and I'm not a full-time engineer
- Shipped my first iOS app, There Lists, to the App Store
- About 12 projects running at the same time
- Earned in X creator payouts by sharing how I use Grok Bot in real life
- Earned in Creator Rewards publishing bot templates
- Found $200 in unclaimed property I'd forgotten about
- Stopped me from paying my sales tax twice
- Caught a failed utility autopay before the due date
- Spotted a 14% jump in my car insurance renewal before it was charged
- Set up real phishing and malware blocking on my iPhone and Mac

The biggest change isn't speed. I stopped carrying everything in my head, and things don't slip anymore.

I still make every call that matters: payments, sends, signatures. I just spend my time deciding instead of doing.

If you're still doing everything yourself, hire a whole team of Grok Bots.

Not America 🇺🇸 Brazil 🇧🇷

Nearly half of everyone shipped across the Atlantic went there. Ten times more than the United States. 🌍

In 1826 Britain made Brazil sign a treaty. The trade would end by 1830. 📜

Brazil signed. Then ignored it. They even had a phrase for laws like that: "para inglês ver". For the English to see. 👀

Tens of thousands of people kept arriving every year. 😔

So Britain changed the law. Brazilian slave ships could now be tried in British courts as pirates. ⚖️

In 1850 the Royal Navy sailed into Brazil's ports, under the guns of the forts. They cut out the slave ships and burned them. 🚢

Emperor Pedro II's government had a choice. War with Britain. Or end the trade. ⚔️

That September, Brazil banned it. Within two years the trade was dead. 🕊️

Yet today only one country is asked to feel ashamed. 🤔

The one that stopped it. 🇬🇧

Be part of us. 🇬🇧

Be Proud Of Us. 🙏🇬🇧

Continuing my Memecoin Recap series, today's focus is robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a 

A lot of people have been asking me to cover this one, and it's arguably one of the hottest tokens on CT right now

Launched on October 29, robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a has already climbed from around $200K to over $4M MC in just two days

But there's more to this project than just price action

I've spent some time digging into its fundamentals, tokenomics, team, and potential catalysts

Here's what I found

1. What is robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a actually building?

robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a isn't simply another memecoin attaching an AI narrative to attract speculative capital

The project calls itself "The First Immortal Protocol," aiming to build a system capable of governing itself, allocating capital autonomously, and operating without constant founder involvement

Sounds ambitious, but the concept is genuinely interesting

The Forever Framework combines AI Agents, governance, and capital allocation into one system

AI Agents compete to propose strategies for deploying treasury capital, including trading, investing, providing liquidity, or funding development

robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a holders vote on which proposals should be approved, while execution agents deploy real treasury capital within predefined limits

Agents that generate value earn rewards and reputation, while holders participating effectively in governance may also receive rewards funded through token buybacks rather than additional inflation

Essentially, Forever is trying to align AI, holders, and capital within a single autonomous ecosystem

If successful, this could evolve into a network of autonomous funds rather than just another AI trading bot

However, this remains the team's intended framework, not a fully operational product

2. Founder background: Is MontBlanc worth paying attention to?

One reason robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a caught my attention is its founder, MontBlanc (@0xMontBlanc), who is described as a co-founder of Camelot, a major DEX within the Arbitrum ecosystem

Camelot has processed tens of billions of dollars in trading volume and generated substantial fees through its AMM infrastructure and DeFi products

MontBlanc has also been associated with launchpad development, DeFi infrastructure, and research into agent-based funds

If his reported involvement is fully verified, that's a meaningful advantage

Personally, I prefer founders with experience building products that have real users rather than teams making ambitious promises without a track record

That said, building a successful DEX and developing an autonomous fund are two completely different challenges

Forever still needs to prove its governance, agent execution, risk management, and treasury protection mechanisms

So I see the founder's background as a positive signal, not a guarantee of success

3. Tokenomics and the Founding NFT allocation

This is where things become particularly interesting

robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a launched with an initial fixed supply of 1B tokens, distributed as follows :

> 40% allocated to Founding Member NFTs
> 10% allocated to the treasury
> 50% associated with the public launch and bonding curve

Before launch, the team minted 500 Founding Member NFTs at 0.045 ETH each, with every NFT receiving an allocation of 800,000 robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a 

That represents 400M tokens, or 40% of the original supply

Reportedly, more than 15,000 whitelist applications competed for just 500 spots, generating significant attention before public trading

But there's another side to this

At a $4M FDV based on the original supply, each 800K allocation would be worth approximately $3,200, compared with a mint cost of only 0.045 ETH

Early participants could therefore be sitting on substantial paper profits

I don't automatically consider this bearish. Rewarding early supporters is normal in crypto

However, 40% of supply is significant, especially after a roughly 20x move from the public launch valuation

I'd want to know how much has been claimed, whether vesting applies, and whether major NFT holders are accumulating or distributing

The team also announced that approximately 10% of the original supply had been bought back and burned

That's positive if fully verified on-chain, but sustainable buybacks matter far more than a one-time burn

4. Partnership with $ORBIO

On October 30, Forever announced a partnership with $ORBIO, which provides AI inference infrastructure

Under the proposed integration, Orbio will offer discounted inference services to Forever's AI Agents, initially through the Forever Venture Fund

It could eventually become the default compute provider for funds launched through the Forever Framework

This partnership makes sense technically

Autonomous agents need reliable, affordable inference to process information and make decisions continuously

It's more relevant than a random partnership announced purely for hype

However, infrastructure availability doesn't mean the agents are already operational, nor does it guarantee profitable strategies

I consider this a positive step toward execution, but actual usage data is still needed

5. Smart money and CT attention

One interesting detail is that Aurelius, a trader previously associated with significant profits on $CATE, is currently holding approximately 25M robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a according to the wallet snapshot I've been tracking

Worth watching, but smart money holdings alone don't validate a thesis

What interests me more is the project's current attention across CT 

Most discussions still appear to originate from the team, particularly @forevercultfund and @0xMontBlanc

Some smaller and mid-tier trading accounts have mentioned the token, but I haven't found substantial coverage from major KOLs such as Cobie, Hsaka, or Ansem in the search results reviewed

This creates an interesting situation

On one hand, broader KOL attention could provide additional exposure if the team starts delivering meaningful progress

On the other, current interest remains heavily driven by the narrative, Founding NFT community, and price action

Without new catalysts, attention could fade quickly

I don't consider limited KOL coverage inherently bearish, but I also wouldn't assume major influencers will eventually promote it

6. What has the team actually shipped?

This is probably the most important part of the research.

So far, the team has delivered or announced several early milestones:

> Token launched on schedule on October 29
> Founding NFT mint completed
> Launch mechanism implemented through Frontier's Uniswap v4 hook
> Approximately 10% supply burn announced.
> Orbio partnership revealed

These are encouraging early developments

However, the core Forever Framework still lacks publicly verifiable operational results

I haven't seen evidence of AI Agents proposing real investment strategies, holders approving capital allocation mandates, or execution agents deploying treasury funds with measurable performance

Governance also appears to remain preliminary, with an early vote focused on the rewards schedule rather than an actual investment mandate

Important details remain unclear, including capital limits, profit calculations, emergency stop mechanisms, reward distribution, and drawdown controls

An autonomous fund needs more than AI Agents capable of trading. It needs effective risk management to protect treasury capital

Until those mechanisms are demonstrated, I still consider robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a an experimental project

The team has delivered the launch, but the hardest part is still ahead

7. Upcoming catalysts

For me, the biggest catalyst isn't another partnership or another smart money wallet buying

It's the actual rollout of the Forever Framework

The team stated that deployment would begin in the week following launch

What I want to see is straightforward: AI Agents submitting real proposals, holders voting on mandates, and execution agents deploying treasury capital on-chain

Ideally, the team should also publish transparent performance data, including profits, losses, and capital efficiency

Other potential catalysts include additional partnerships, governance rewards, further buybacks, and eventually allowing third parties to launch their own Forever Funds

But execution remains the deciding factor

If the team delivers on schedule, the market will have stronger grounds to reassess the project

If updates remain mostly narrative-driven without tangible progress, attention could decline quickly

8. Price action and market cap levels

At the time of my review, robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a was trading around $3.7M–$4.1M MC

The chart shows a bullish structure, with relatively shallow pullbacks followed by new highs

Exactly the kind of price action degens love

However, after a roughly 20x move in two days, I'm not particularly interested in chasing 

A significant amount of short-term optimism may already be priced in

I'm watching two potential scenarios

The first is a pullback toward $3M–$3.3M MC, followed by convincing buying pressure. This could become an interesting retest if the bullish structure holds

The second is a deeper correction toward $2M–$2.5M MC, which could offer a more attractive risk/reward setup if the thesis remains intact, liquidity stays healthy, and major wallets aren't aggressively distributing

If market cap loses $2M with increasing sell volume, I'd reassess rather than blindly catch the bottom

Conversely, a strong breakout above $4M–$4.2M could open another phase of price discovery

Still, I wouldn't set overly ambitious targets without clearer evidence of product execution and sustained capital inflows

With a token this new, discipline matters more than predicting the next top

9. My overall assessment

After researching robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a, I think it's more interesting than many tokens currently riding the AI narrative

What I like is the autonomous governance concept, the founder's reported DeFi background, the incentive structure, and the technically relevant Orbio partnership

Limited major KOL coverage also leaves room for broader attention if the project begins delivering real progress

However, three concerns prevent me from becoming overly bullish

First, 40% of the initial supply went to Founding NFT holders, potentially creating significant selling pressure from low-cost allocations

Second, the core framework has no established operational track record. We still don't know whether agents can generate sustainable returns, governance will work effectively, or treasury capital will be adequately protected

Third, the valuation has already increased substantially in a very short period, making FOMO entries less attractive from a risk/reward perspective

I don't think it's fair to FUD robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a simply because its product isn't finished. The token only launched two days ago

But I'm also not calling it a long-term gem based solely on the founder's background, one partnership, and a few smart money wallets

My current view is simple

robinhood:0xacc8de336f5d2366fa7334383d8fab73499f582a is an interesting early-stage narrative bet worth monitoring, with meaningful upside potential if the team delivers what it has promised

I'd rather wait for a reasonable pullback or clearer evidence of framework execution before considering an entry

Over the next few days, I'm more interested in whether AI Agents actually begin operating, governance mandates go live, and treasury capital gets deployed than whether the market cap breaks $5M

A strong narrative can send a token flying

But execution is what determines whether it survives

One of the best posts I've seen here for a while 🎯

I'm bored to death of reading stuff like this from famous indie hackers.

Every few weeks, someone with a big following decides they're suddenly expert on a topic they Googled last week. Out comes a confident thread with a polished breakdown, bold claims, and zero nuance as if they've spent years in the field.

In reality, they know a couple of surface-level facts. That's it. Scratch one layer deeper and there's nothing there.

And the worst part isn't them. It's the thousands of followers nodding along, bookmarking it, quoting it, repeating it as gospel. Nobody questions it because "he built a $20k MRR app, so he must know"

Shipping a successful product doesn't make you an authority on everything. Audience size ≠ expertise.

Not every post is garbage and not every big account does this. But it happens way too often and people are making real decisions based on half-baked takes.
